description: Bring your own video, audio or image into a project — not generated, yours. Two ways: `media_url` (a public http(s) address; the server fetches it, max 100 MB) or `file_name` + `content_type` (you get a signed `upload_url` and the `header` that are part of its signature: PUT the file's raw bytes there within the hour with EXACTLY those headers — the answer's `anleitung` has the ready curl line; a missing header is a 403). Either way the answer is the `asset_key` — use it in lab_timeline_apply as clips[].asset_key (video) or bett.asset_key (audio). Exception: in projects that check images, an uploaded image is not in the project after the PUT — the answer then carries `abschluss_noetig` and an `abschluss_key`; after the PUT call lab_add_media again with the same project_id, art, herkunft and `abschluss_key` only. That call checks the image and returns the `asset_key`, or says why it was refused. Free. Internal addresses are refused.

abschluss_key.description: Only after an upload whose answer said `abschluss_noetig`: the `abschluss_key` from that answer, given AFTER the PUT returned 200. Give it instead of media_url and file_name

content_type.description: Media type of the upload, e.g. video/mp4, audio/mpeg — required with file_name

file_name.description: Name of a local file to upload, with extension. Give this OR media_url

herkunft.description: Required, no default: 'eigen' = shot, recorded or made by people (no AI generation); 'ki' = generated or altered with AI. Decides the EU AI Act Art. 50 disclosure of every export that uses this file. If the file itself carries an AI mark (C2PA or IPTC source type), it stays AI material whatever you declare, and the answer says so.

media_url.description: Public http(s) URL of the file. Give this OR file_name

project_id.description: Project id (from lab_list_projects) — positive integer as string

name: lab_add_media
title: Add Media
